nodes.title: How to use — W5 v16 (PRODUCTION 2/3)
widgets_values:
## W5 v16 — first frame + video (PRODUCTION 2/3)
Fast production version (approved v15, CHANGELOG #47). The skeleton comes ready from the catalog; this workflow does not extract poses.

**Fill in:**
1. **Video name** — `<product>_<pose>` (e.g. `caramel-tank-jeans_look-02`). Becomes the output folder.
2. **Product** — front photo, full body, model wearing the garment.
3. **Catalog POSE** — `motion/poses/<pose>/pose.mp4`. It shows up in the list after running W1 and `catalog.py pose <pose>`.

The pose for the first frame is frame 0 of the same pose.mp4.

**Output** in `output/motion/production/<name>/`: `frame0_*.png` (1088×1920) and `video_*.mp4` (896×1600, 124 frames, 24 fps).
**Time:** ~8.5 min on an RTX 4090 from a cold start (frame0 ~3 min, video ~3.5 min, loads ~2 min).

**What makes it fast:** turbo LoRA 8 steps (switch *Turbo* OFF = 20 steps, slower, slightly sharper face) · ControlNet strength 0.6 / end 0.5 (with turbo, stronger values paint the skeleton on the body) · INT8 attention on both models (nodes *Attention*, set to `pytorch attention` to turn off).

**Then:** `catalog.py compare <name> <pose>` (original | skeleton | generated) and `catalog.py upscale <name>` for W6.

Tip: right-click a group title → *Set Group Nodes to Never/Always* to turn a stage off.
